1.why: All seven screens are static cards with no animations, carousels or pop-up dialogs; the only busy element is the dark Logs panel that appends technical text.

2.why: Each screen has a large bold heading, a highlighted status banner and a single filled teal primary button, so the key action stands out, though the dark log block competes visually.

3.why: One task per screen makes navigation easy, but on step 2 the needed recovery code is buried in a monospace developer log alongside a 64-character hex token and URL, which is hard to locate/copy.

4.why: The persistent 5-step progress chips and 'next step' banners reduce memory load, yet she must still carry a long code from the log panel and remember multi-part password rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol).

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, no autofill hint, no password-manager/passkey option or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced — no saved/masked email shown back to her, no remembered account or device; only the layout itself repeats.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain and reassuring ('Start when you are ready', 'Password saved. Sign in when you are ready.') in a large, high-contrast font.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the seven screenshots, so problem-plus-fix error messaging cannot be observed; only success banners exist.

9.why: The password rules are stated in words but no example password is given, the email field has no placeholder example, and no sample code format is shown for the code fields.

10.why: The available options are clearly labelled ('Verify code' vs 'Send a new recovery code', 'Open your simulated recovery link', password sign-in, verification code), although no biometric/face option exists.

11.why: Every screen presents at most two buttons plus one 'Need help?' link, keeping choice load minimal.

12.why: Each step opens with an explicit outcome banner ('Code verified. Now choose your new password.', 'Privacy statement accepted...') and the Logs panel confirms events.

13.why: A 'Need help?' link is present on all screens and each step includes a short guiding tip such as 'Take your time: this step will stay here until you are ready.'

14.why: A 'Send a new recovery code' retry path exists and there is no session countdown, but there is no visible back/edit link to return to an earlier step or correct a mistyped email.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the identical header, step-chip bar, banner, form, button, help link and Logs layout with the same colours and typography.
